name: Peter Pan's Flight
sensoryNotes: Suspended dark ride flying over London and Neverland with vibrant UV blacklight effects.
adhdTip: Continuous moving boarding belt. Very popular; aim for early rope drop or during the fireworks.

name: Pirates of the Caribbean
sensoryNotes: Indoor boat voyage featuring atmospheric battle cannon fire, battle sounds, two minor drops, and low lighting.
adhdTip: Ear defenders advised during the fortress cannonade. Queue area is dark, cool, and immersive.

name: Big Thunder Mountain
sensoryNotes: Fast runaway mine train with roaring track audio, sudden sharp turns, and underground tunnel plunges.
adhdTip: Queue line can echo loudly under the timber shelter. Use single rider or Premier Access if sensory threshold is low.

name: Phantom Manor
sensoryNotes: Gothic ghost tour with stretching portrait rooms, spooky orchestrations, glowing skeletons, and total blackouts.
adhdTip: Pre-show room has a brief moment of complete darkness and a thunderclap scream.

name: Star Wars Hyperspace Mountain
sensoryNotes: High-speed indoor coaster with catapult launch, full inversions, strobe laser fire, and blaring John Williams soundtrack.
adhdTip: High physical intensity. Best ridden when fully prepared for sensory overload and headrest vibrations.

name: it's a small world
sensoryNotes: Gentle, colourful canal cruise with singing animatronic dolls. Bright, pastel lighting throughout.
adhdTip: Repetitive catchy theme tune; ideal low-intensity sensory decompression ride.

name: The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror
sensoryNotes: Accelerated vertical freefall elevator drops with intense stomach-drop sensations, ghostly projections, and loud metallic sound effects.
adhdTip: Very high fear factor. Prepare children for sudden weightlessness and random drop sequences.

name: Crush's Coaster
sensoryNotes: Spinning turtle shell coaster plunging through the dark East Australian Current. Unpredictable centrifugal spins.
adhdTip: Outdoor queue moves slowly and lacks shade. Visualise the spinning motion with children beforehand.

name: Ratatouille: The Adventure
sensoryNotes: Trackless 3D glasses ride with heat/cold physical blasts, water sprays, and quick scurrying motions.
adhdTip: 3D glasses can be removed if visual simulation triggers dizziness without ruining the experience.

name: Avengers Assemble: Flight Force
sensoryNotes: High-velocity inverted launch coaster with Iron Man & Captain Marvel LED screens in near-total darkness.
adhdTip: Launch accelerates from 0 to 60mph in under 3 seconds; check headrest positioning carefully.

name: Spider-Man W.E.B. Adventure
sensoryNotes: Interactive 3D screen attraction requiring repetitive arm movements to sling virtual webs at Spider-Bots.
adhdTip: Highly engaging and tactile; fantastic for active kids needing physical participation.

name: TOGETHER: a Pixar Musical Adventure
sensoryNotes: West End-quality live indoor theatre featuring an eight-piece live orchestra, multi-sensory water droplets, scent effects, and moving stage screens.
adhdTip: Air-conditioned theatre with tiered seating; arrive 25 minutes before showtime for central sightlines.

name: The Lion King: Rhythms of the Pride Lands
sensoryNotes: Acrobatic musical spectacular with high-decibel live drumming, aerialists swinging over the audience, and vibrant lighting rigs.
adhdTip: Sensory-rich and loud. Ear defenders recommended for kids sensitive to booming bass drum percussions.

name: Mickey and the Magician
sensoryNotes: Broadway-calibre musical stage illusions with classic Disney showtunes, tap dancing, and bright stage spotlights.
adhdTip: Captivating rapid scene changes keep young attention spans fully focused from start to finish.

name: Disney Stars on Parade
sensoryNotes: Daytime outdoor parade with loud mobile sound systems, costumed characters, and a mechanical dragon breathing real fire.
adhdTip: Crowds form 45 minutes ahead along Main Street. Stand near 'it's a small world' for quicker exits.

name: Disney Tales of Magic Nighttime Spectacular
sensoryNotes: Castle projection show accompanied by drone swarms, laser arrays, pyrotechnic explosions, and high-volume cinematic orchestrations.
adhdTip: Very packed viewing areas. Stand back toward the Central Plaza hub or Main Street train station for easier escape routes.
